issues.t: Four-speed automatic slips, flares or fails
issues.sym: The engine revs up between shifts, the van hesitates to move, shifts late or harshly, or loses some gears or reverse. Heavy loads make it worse.
issues.why: The GM four-speed automatics in these vans (4L60-E in lighter models, 4L80-E in heavy-duty ones) wear internally from heat and weight. Work vans that carry cargo or tow all day are especially hard on them.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. Dark, burnt-smelling fluid points to internal wear. Lighten the load, avoid towing, and get a transmission shop diagnosis; a rebuild or replacement is the usual fix. An extra transmission cooler helps on working vans.

issues.t: Radiator leaks coolant into the transmission
issues.sym: Shifts start to slip or shudder, and the transmission fluid looks pink and milky, like a strawberry milkshake. The coolant level may drop too.
issues.why: The transmission fluid cooler sits inside the radiator. When the wall between them cracks, coolant mixes into the transmission fluid and quickly destroys the clutches. An owner reported needing a radiator and a transmission at about 44,000 miles.
issues.next: If the fluid looks milky, stop driving and have it checked at once. Replace the radiator right away; if caught early, a full fluid flush may save the transmission, but often it needs a rebuild.

issues.t: Engine leaks coolant from intake manifold gaskets
issues.sym: Coolant keeps disappearing, there's dried coolant crust at the top of the engine under the doghouse cover, or the oil turns milky.
issues.why: The Vortec V6 and V8 engines of this era use intake gaskets that break down with heat and DEX-COOL coolant, letting coolant leak outside or into the oil.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level and check the oil for a milky look. Replace the gaskets with updated ones before coolant damages the engine bearings, and change the oil after the repair.

issues.t: Misfires from the central 'spider' fuel injector
issues.sym: Rough idle, misfire codes, hesitation, a raw fuel smell or a long crank when starting.
issues.why: These engines use one central injector body with small lines to each cylinder. The nozzles stick or leak over time, upsetting the fuel mix in some cylinders.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes and fuel pressure checked. Replacing the spider assembly with the updated design is the standard repair.

issues.t: Fuel pump wears out and van won't start
issues.sym: Long cranking before it starts, sputtering under load, or the engine dies and won't restart.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pump wears out on these vans, and a clogged fuel filter adds strain. Delayed starting was the most-reported problem on the 2000 Savana.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested. If the pump is weak, replace the pump module and fuel filter together.

issues.t: Transmission fluid leaks
issues.sym: Red fluid drips under the middle of the van, the fluid level drops, and shifting gets sloppy if it runs low.
issues.why: Pan gaskets, cooler lines and seals on high-mileage vans start to leak. Owners report major repairs at around 130,000 miles.
issues.next: Find the leak early and keep the fluid topped up; running it low ruins the transmission. Cooler lines and pan gaskets are simple fixes.

issues.t: 4.3L V6 uses too much oil
issues.sym: You need to add oil between changes, see blue smoke at startup, or find fouled spark plugs.
issues.why: The 4.3L V6 in these vans is known to burn oil as the piston rings wear and the PCV system clogs.
issues.next: Check the oil level every fill-up. A PCV service is a simple first step; heavy oil use may mean ring wear.

issues.t: Ticking from broken exhaust manifold bolts
issues.sym: A ticking or puffing sound from the engine, loudest on a cold start, and sometimes an exhaust smell in the cab.
issues.why: Exhaust manifold bolts on the 6.0L V8 snap from repeated heating and cooling, letting exhaust leak at the manifold.
issues.next: Have the manifold checked for leaks. Fix it before exhaust fumes enter the cab; broken bolts may need to be drilled out.

issues.t: Duramax diesel runs hot under load
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs when towing, climbing hills or hauling in hot weather, and power may drop.
issues.why: The LLY Duramax has limited cooling capacity for heavy work, and a weak fan clutch or a dirty radiator makes it worse.
issues.next: Ease off and let it cool if the gauge climbs. Have the fan clutch, radiator and intercooler checked and cleaned.

issues.t: Diesel particulate filter clogs
issues.sym: A message about the exhaust filter, the check engine light, frequent regeneration, or a loss of power.
issues.why: The LMM Duramax's soot filter needs regular highway driving to clean itself. Short trips and idling, common for work vans, let soot build up.
issues.next: Take it for a long highway drive if the dash asks for a regeneration. If the light stays on, a shop can run a forced cleaning or clean the filter.

issues.t: Diesel high-pressure fuel pump can fail and contaminate the fuel system
issues.sym: The engine suddenly loses power, stalls, or cranks without starting, sometimes after a fuel-pressure warning.
issues.why: The CP4 high-pressure pump on the LGH Duramax can wear internally, especially with poor or watery fuel, sending metal through the injectors and fuel lines.
issues.next: Stop driving if it loses power or won't start. Use clean fuel and change the fuel filter on time. A failed pump usually means replacing the pump, injectors and lines.

issues.t: Eight-speed automatic shifts harshly or slips
issues.sym: Hard downshifts, clunks when coming to a stop, slipping in low gears, or hesitation before it goes into gear.
issues.why: The eight-speed automatic used with the 4.3L V6 and 2.8L diesel has known problems with valve body wear and shift adaptation.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about GM bulletins and software updates for shift quality. If the problem continues, the valve body or other parts may need replacing.

issues.t: 2.8L diesel turbo whines or leaks oil at the ducts
issues.sym: A whistling or whining noise under load, oily residue around the turbo hoses, or reduced power.
issues.why: Loose turbo duct clamps or a worn turbocharger on the 2.8L Duramax cause boost leaks and noise.
issues.next: Have the turbo ducts and clamps inspected. A loose clamp is a simple fix; a worn turbo needs replacing.

issues.t: Fuel pump control module fails and engine stalls or won't shut off
issues.sym: Crank but no start with the check engine light on, rough running, or the fuel pump, starter or accessories staying on after you shut the van off.
issues.why: The module that powers the fuel pump can short internally. GM issued a bulletin for these vans and covers the part under federal emissions warranty for 8 years or 80,000 miles.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. If the van won't start or acts strangely when shut off, have a GMC dealer check for codes P023F or P129F. The module replacement is often covered.

issues.t: Transmission software can cause harsh shifts or rear wheel lockup (recall)
issues.sym: Harsh shifts, sudden loss of power or slowing, or in rare cases rear wheel lockup or unexpected movement.
issues.why: Incorrect transmission control software was installed on some vans, so GM recalled them for a free update.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and have the software update done at a GMC dealer.

issues.t: Unused rear heater wiring can corrode and overheat on cutaways (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or melted wiring near the driver-side door pillar. Often no warning before damage.
issues.why: On cutaway chassis vans, an unused rear blower circuit is left with exposed connectors that can corrode, overheat and start a fire. GM recalled about 150,000 vans.
issues.next: If you own a Savana cutaway (box truck, shuttle bus or RV base), check your VIN for this recall. Dealers seal the circuit for free.

issues.t: Power window switch can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell, smoke or heat from the driver's door switch, or windows that stop working.
issues.why: Liquid can get into the power window switch and cause a short that overheats it. GM recalled the vans.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If you smell burning from the door, stop and have it checked.

issues.t: Rear climate control wiring can short and burn (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from the headliner area, or rear climate controls that stop working.
issues.why: Wiring for the rear climate control module can short and overheat, which could start a fire in the headliner.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer repair is free.

issues.t: Tires can lose tread or blow out (recall)
issues.sym: Bulges on the sidewall, vibration, or sudden air loss at speed.
issues.why: Some tires were over-cured at the factory, so the sidewall or belts can break apart.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the tires inspected or replaced free.

issues.t: Positive battery cable can short (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke near the battery, or electrical problems.
issues.why: The positive battery cable terminal can short against nearby parts, raising fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer will fix it free.

issues.t: Drive belt squeals, breaks or causes a hard start
issues.sym: A squealing belt, a hard start or no start, or sudden loss of power steering and power brake assist.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for belt squeal and broken belts on these vans, which can strand the van and take away steering and brake assist.
issues.next: If the belt squeals, have it and the tensioner checked soon. If you lose steering or brake assist, pull over safely.

issues.t: Check engine light from a false trouble code
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on but the van runs normally.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for a software issue that can set an incorrect trouble code.
issues.next: Have a dealer read the code and check for the bulletin. A software fix is usually covered under warranty.

issues.t: Steering gear nut may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or looseness in the steering. In the worst case, steering control can be lost.
issues.why: A nut on the steering gear may not have been tightened properly at the factory. GM recalled 2025–2026 vans, then recalled some again when parts were missed.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls, even if the first steering recall was already done. If the steering feels loose, don't drive until it's inspected.

issues.t: Driver door impact beam may have bad welds (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. The door may not protect you as well in a side crash.
issues.why: The steel beam inside the driver's door may have improper welds on a small number of vans.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer will replace the door free.

issues.t: Passenger head restraint may be poorly welded (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms in normal driving; the head restraint may not protect properly in a rear crash.
issues.why: The front passenger head restraint may be badly welded to the seat frame on a small number of vans.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer will inspect and replace the seat frame free.

issues.t: Check engine light with code P062B
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes with no change in how the van drives.
issues.why: GM issued preliminary information to dealers about this code, which relates to the engine computer's injector control. Engineers were still investigating.
issues.next: Have a dealer read the code. It should be covered under the new-vehicle warranty.

issues.t: Van can roll away after shifting out of Park (recalls)
issues.sym: The shifter moves out of Park without the brake pressed, or the key comes out when not in Park.
issues.why: Two recalls covered a shift interlock defect that could let the van roll away.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Brakes pulsate from hot spots on the rotors
issues.sym: Shaking or pulsation through the pedal or steering wheel when braking, sometimes at low mileage.
issues.why: Heavy vans heat the brake rotors, causing hot spots and uneven wear. Owners report needing repairs at around 16,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured. Replace them with good-quality rotors and pads.

issues.t: Alternator can short and start an engine fire (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from the engine area, or charging warnings.
issues.why: An internal short in the voltage regulator could heat up enough to start a fire.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for open recalls and get it repaired free.

issues.t: Transmission defect can stall the van on the road (recall)
issues.sym: The van may stall or lose drive while driving.
issues.why: GM recalled some vans for a transmission defect that could leave them stalled on the road.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Interior door handle or armrest breaks off
issues.sym: The inside door handle or armrest cracks or comes off in your hand, making the door hard to open or close from inside.
issues.why: Plastic interior door trim and handles break under daily use. Owners report it at fairly low mileage.
issues.next: Replace the handle or armrest. Make sure each door can still open from inside, especially for passengers.

issues.t: Steering and wheel bearing nuts may come loose (recalls)
issues.sym: Unusual steering feel, grinding, pulling under braking, or the ABS not working.
issues.why: Three recalls covered loose pitman arm and tie rod nuts and a loose wheel bearing nut.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; repairs are free.

issues.t: Corroded fuel filler pipe can leak (recall)
issues.sym: Fuel smell or drips near the filler, especially while fueling.
issues.why: The filler pipe can rust through and leak fuel.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, have it checked. Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Power steering cooler hose can leak onto the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaks, a burning smell, or whining steering.
issues.why: A leaking cooler hose could spray fluid onto hot engine parts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Fuel odor or fuel leak (recall)
issues.sym: Fuel smell around the van or visible fuel leak.
issues.why: GM recalled some vans for fuel leakage that could start a fire.
issues.next: Don't drive if you smell fuel. Check your VIN for open recalls.
